objective: P2 Stage 2 (plan v2 section 3.2): reproduce the statistical jump model regime strategy (Shu-Yu-Mulvey 2024) on the US market 1990-2023, sweep nine specifications along inputs, persistence and model class, and test whether the daily regime multiplier raises the exposure-matched Sharpe of the pilot sleeve S3 in the stress window without costing more than 0.10 of recent Sharpe; S1, S2 and C2 are reported.

sources.core_claim: Journal of Asset Management 25(5):493-507 (2024), DOI 10.1057/s41260-024-00376-x. Online 2-state jump model on DD(hl10), Sortino(hl20, hl60), 3000-day training refit every six months, jump penalty chosen monthly by the 0/1 strategy's 8-year validation Sharpe, one-day delay, 10 bp: S&P 500 1990-2023 Sharpe 0.48 -> 0.68, MDD -55.2% -> -26.6%, turnover 44%, average exposure 80%; HMM 0.54, turnover 141%.
sources.project_applicability: Reproduction target (Stage 2a) and the base protocol for every JM specification.
sources.reflection: Authors' own data (Bloomberg total return, GFD 3-month bills); no comparison with volatility targeting; selecting the penalty on validation Sharpe can overfit the validation window. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/arxiv__shu-yu-mulvey-2024-fulltext.txt; journal record reports/research/intel/sources/p2-s2-regime-layer-2026-10-06/princeton-shu-yu-mulvey-2024-jam-record.html.

sources.core_claim: Sparse jump-model regimes per factor index drive a dynamic allocation across seven US long-only indices, test 2007-2024 with 5 bp, improving on the market and on equal weight.
sources.project_applicability: Out-of-sample use of the same persistence machinery on factor sleeves, the closest published analogue of gating our ETF sleeves.
sources.reflection: Same authors; sparse feature selection over about 20 features is beyond this stage's minimum depth. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/arxiv__shu-mulvey-2024-dynamic-factor-allocation-jm.txt.

sources.core_claim: Authors' Apache-2.0 library: loss = 0.5 * squared Euclidean distance; DP values[t] = loss[t] + min(values[t-1] + penalty); online labels = argmin of forward values; k-means++ starts with n_init 10, max_iter 1000, tol 1e-8; states sorted by cumulative return.
sources.project_applicability: Faithful implementation (P-1 item 2) and the cross-check of our module.
sources.reflection: Not installed in the project environment; used read-only from snapshots and an isolated venv. Snapshots reports/research/intel/sources/p2-s2-regime-layer-2026-10-06/github-jumpmodels-jump.py.txt and github-jumpmodels-base.py.txt.

sources.core_claim: Regime-based asset allocation with HMMs can beat static allocation when regimes are persistent and inferred online; the gain depends on persistence and on transaction costs.
sources.project_applicability: Background for the HMM point on the model axis and the role of persistence.

sources.core_claim: Journal of Financial Economics 138 (2020) 95-117: out of sample, volatility-managed versions of most of 103 equity strategies do not beat the unmanaged ones, but momentum strategies improve.
sources.project_applicability: The exposure-matched volatility target is a non-trivial control for a momentum sleeve such as S3; the regime layer must beat it, not only buy-and-hold.
sources.reflection: US factor portfolios, monthly; not levered ETFs. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/cederburg-2020-volmanaged-jfe.txt.

sources.core_claim: Momentum crashes are concentrated in panic states after bear markets with high volatility and are partly forecastable; a dynamic strategy using bear-state and volatility forecasts roughly doubles the momentum Sharpe ratio.
sources.project_applicability: Mechanism for state dependence of a momentum rotation such as S3 and for why a bear-and-volatility state can add to a pure volatility target.
sources.reflection: Cross-sectional stock momentum, not ETF rotation. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/daniel-moskowitz-2016-momentum-crashes.txt.

sources.core_claim: Leveraged ETF compounding depends on return autocorrelation and regime: trends enhance returns, mean reversion and volatility clustering induce underperformance (about 20 years of SPY and QQQ data).
sources.project_applicability: Why removing levered exposure in choppy high-volatility bear regimes could raise S3's Sharpe by more than scaling it down.
sources.reflection: Abstract read; no trading rule tested. Snapshot reports/research/intel/sources/regime-cycle-2026-10-04/arxiv__letf-compounding-regime-2504.20116.txt.

sources.core_claim: Copenhagen Business School MSc thesis (2025): regime-aware factor ETF strategies 2017-2025 delivered higher returns, Sharpe and lower drawdowns than benchmarks, but the observed performance gains lack statistical significance.
sources.project_applicability: Independent recent evidence that effects of this kind are small relative to sampling error in 8-year windows; the power section treats the sleeve thresholds as policy thresholds.

sources.core_claim: On 2016-01..2023-09 the SMA200 and credit-ratio gates on S3 did not beat exposure-matched volatility-target controls (Sharpe 0.78-0.81 vs gates 0.34-0.85) or 18 of 20 circular shifts; single specifications, lagging price trends.
sources.project_applicability: The control and placebo design this stage reuses; the new elements are persistence-penalised online clustering, 30+ years of fitting history and the depth sweep.
sources.reflection: Shallow single-spec test under the owner's 10-04 depth rule; it cannot refute the regime layer.
